label: Elimination Theory
notes: This chapter runs from printed pages 121 through 176 and applies Grobner bases to solving systems. Elimination theory systematically removes variables from a system of polynomial equations, reducing it to fewer variables so that solutions can be found by back-substitution, much as Gaussian elimination triangulates a linear system.

label: Elimination and Extension
notes: The elimination ideal collects all consequences of a system that involve only the later variables. The Elimination Theorem says a lexicographic Grobner basis instantly exposes this ideal, while the Extension Theorem governs when a partial solution of the eliminated system extends to a full solution upstairs.

label: Lex Order Eliminates
notes: With lexicographic order the Grobner basis is structured so that some generators involve only the variables we wish to keep. Intersecting the basis with the smaller polynomial ring yields the elimination ideal directly, turning the geometric act of projecting away variables into a purely mechanical computation.

label: Geometry of Elimination
notes: Geometrically, eliminating variables projects a variety onto a coordinate subspace. The projection's closure is the variety of the elimination ideal, but the projection itself may miss points where leading coefficients vanish. The Extension Theorem characterizes precisely which partial solutions lift back to the full variety.

label: Implicitization
notes: A parametrized surface or curve can be converted to defining equations by elimination. Introducing the parameters as extra variables and eliminating them produces the implicit polynomial equations of the image, solving the implicitization problem central to computer-aided geometric design and modeling.

label: Resultants
notes: The resultant of two polynomials is a single polynomial in their coefficients that vanishes exactly when they share a common root. Resultants give a determinant-based route to elimination, complementing Grobner bases and providing explicit degree bounds. Next: the algebra-geometry dictionary.
